ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Suppose that in the future humans land on Mars. After the astronauts finish their investigation, when they take a spacecraft to return from Mars to Earth, they undergo the orbital transfer process shown in the figure. When the spacecraft moves on orbit II, what is the relationship between the speeds when passing point P and point Q?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the spacecraft moves on orbit II, its speed when passing point P is greater than its speed when passing point Q
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, Mars is located on the right side, and three dashed orbits are marked: orbit I is near Mars, orbit II is a larger elliptical orbit, and orbit III is farther outside. Two points are marked on orbit II: point P is on the right side of Mars, close to Mars; point Q is on the left side of Mars, clearly farther from Mars than point P. Reasoning: When the spacecraft moves on orbit II, it can be regarded as moving along the same elliptical orbit under the dominance of Mars's gravity. On an elliptical orbit, at a position close to the central celestial body, gravitational potential energy is smaller, kinetic energy is larger, and speed is greater; at a position far from the central celestial body, speed is smaller. Therefore the speed at point P is greater than the speed at point Q.
